competitive_landscape: The water is served by Muttrah dhow cruises, Daymaniyat dive and dolphin boats, and Khasab fjord dhows — tourist excursions rather than transport. There is no fast coastal corridor linking Muscat to Sur or to the Musandam fjords, despite a dramatic and underused coastline.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Sheltered coastal hops — Muttrah · Al Mouj · Bandar Khairan · Daymaniyat — all-electric, with no new charging infrastructure beyond a berth pedestal.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Opens the long Oman corridors (Sur / Ras Al Hadd) and the cross-Gulf line to the UAE via Musandam / Khasab as single hybrid legs, with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates clean foiling mobility as a destination differentiator for coastal and island tourism.

regulatory_note: Marine activity falls under Oman's maritime authorities and ASYAD, within Oman Vision 2040's tourism-growth agenda — a supportive frame for a premium clean coastal fleet and fjord access.
seasonality: The Gulf of Oman off Muscat is calm Oct–Apr (peak season) and hotter and more humid Jun–Sep; the khareef monsoon affects Salalah in the far south, not Muscat. Coastal and island waters are operable most of the year.
signature_routes: Muscat ↔ Sur / Ras Al Hadd (coastal long-haul)

summary: Muscat strings along a rugged coast of bays, marinas and protected islands — Muttrah, Al Mouj, Bandar Khairan, the Daymaniyat reserve — with the Sur / Ras Al Hadd turtle coast to the southeast. Pioneer II suits the sheltered coastal hops; Quanta-LR's hybrid range opens the long Oman corridors and the cross-Gulf line to the UAE via Musandam (Khasab).
tagline: A dramatic coastline of coves and islands — and the gateway to Musandam.
transit_planning: For an authority: a premium, zero-emission coastal marine layer that knits Muscat's dispersed waterfront nodes together and reaches the iconic-but-isolated Musandam and Ras Al Hadd destinations — additive to existing transport.

use_cases.body: Fast, smooth foiling between Muttrah, Al Mouj, Bandar Khairan and the Daymaniyat reserve — comfortable in the swell that pounds conventional craft.
